title: Assertion-Aware Observation in AID Cycle
summary: Embedded-conclusion detection (user assertions that embed framing, architectural, or design conclusions, with or without confidence markers) is an AID inline observation responsibility rather than a separate UserPromptSubmit pattern-matching hook, because lexical pattern matching was found to be both over-inclusive and under-inclusive. When the agent semantically detects an embedded conclusion near an artifact-production moment, it deploys open-question reframing from the question toolkit. This is a Tier 2 context-responsive mechanism that trades pre-prompt Architectural Isolation for semantic detection, relying on Tier 1 backstops (Susceptibility Snapshot, Framing Audit) to catch what inline detection misses.
workflow_point: AID cycle Attend phase, at or near artifact-production moments
mechanism: semantic embedded-conclusion detection with open-question reframing

links.note: Extends the AID cycle's Attend phase (ADR-040) with embedded-conclusion detection as an additional susceptibility signal.
Deploys open-question reframing from the Question Toolkit (ADR-056) as the response when an embedded conclusion is detected.
Extends ADR-057's susceptibility-signal repertoire with embedded conclusions as a new signal type, detected inline rather than via a separate hook.
Classified as a Tier 2 context-responsive mechanism under ADR-058's two-tier floor, since it requires agent judgment about what constitutes a concerning assertion.
Names the Framing Audit (ADR-061) as a structural backstop providing isolated evaluation that catches embedded conclusions this ADR's inline detection misses.
